summaries: Backlog review manifests read links as the vault gate does: code spans and fenced code, such as a `[[...resource]]` route file, are never review sources, embeds resolve as the vault file they name, upstream notes keep the alias-free links their compilers write, and an approved upstream note with unparsable link text is listed in `unparsed_link_sources` instead of failing every manifest; review Evidence, accepted minor findings and the headless absent-input check no longer read code as a link.

Role agents take their model and reasoning effort from per-host execution profile tables (`platforms/<host>/execution-profiles.json`, profile `auto`) whose defaults keep today's settings, and Codex setup accepts `--execution-profile inherit` so every role follows the parent session; the Claude Code host contract documents the equivalent session setting.

`backlog_compile.py stub-story` writes `uses_design` and `constrained_by` only when they have a value, so the per-write vault check no longer rejects the compiler's own stub of a story without design or constraint references as an empty typed relation list.
